summary: The payment failures are caused by the expiry of payment-service's bank-facing mTLS client certificate (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal, notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z), which banks' TLS layer now rejects with alert 45 (expired certificate), so outbound fund transfers can no longer reach bank-partner-api. Confidence is high (0.78, the critic's cap), anchored on two independent signals in the same 12:12-12:19Z window: a second-precision log onset (first mTLS rejection 12:15:27Z, 27s after notAfter) and a collapse of bank_api_error_rate to 100% and payment_success_rate to ~2.4%. The "green" error-rate dashboard is literally correct but blind, because failed transfers are marked PENDING_RETRY on a non-HTTP settlement/retry path rather than returned as 5xx. Both in-window changes (cfg-2502 at 11:20Z, dep-5510 at 10:30Z) are time- and mechanism-inconsistent with onset, and no competing explanation names a different origin.

ranked_hypotheses.title: payment-service bank-facing mTLS client cert expired at 12:15:00Z
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The client certificate 'CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal' used by payment-service to authenticate to the external bank-partner-api expired at notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z. Immediately after expiry (first rejected handshake 12:15:27Z), every mTLS handshake to the bank was rejected, so outbound fund transfers could no longer reach the partner. Failed transfers were marked PENDING_RETRY inside the settlement/retry path rather than returned as HTTP 5xx, so the HTTP error-rate panel stayed flat (~0.22%) while payment_success_rate collapsed to ~2.4%. Confidence is set at the critic's cap (0.78) rather than higher because the key linkage hop — that the expired credential is specifically the one bound to the payment-service->bank-partner-api edge — is inferred from log-line wording, not confirmed against a cert subject/key binding or a cert-lifecycle source.

causal_chain.claim: Client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z reaches expiry at 12:15Z
All mTLS handshakes from payment-service to bank-partner-api are rejected from 12:15:27Z onward (first NEW error, 27s after notAfter)
bank_api_error_rate jumps to 57.23% in the 12:12Z bucket then 100% from 12:19Z; payment_success_rate falls to ~2.4%
Failed transfers are marked PENDING_RETRY (a non-HTTP settlement/retry path), so the HTTP error-rate panel remains flat at ~0.22% (75 ERROR vs 1 WARN)
Customers observe ~40 failed fund transfers; success rate ~2.4% corroborates them; the error persists unchanged through 13:58Z (no rotation)

assumptions: The expired cert is the credential on the payment-service->bank-partner-api edge — supported by the revoked-cert line naming OUR client cert (F20) and the rejection direction (alert 45 to us, F25), but not confirmed by a cert registry (none exists, F26) nor by a renewal/reload event (F23).

A still-valid cert being rejected by the partner, or a renewed cert loaded against a stale partner truststore, would produce a similar log signature; no partner-side telemetry exists to rule this out (F22, F28).

The failure is confined to payment-service: bank-partner-api is external/shared=false with no other visible callers (F16, F17); unmeasured co-tenant degradation of ledger-db/kafka would widen blast radius but cannot change the origin.
Metric onset in the 12:12Z bucket (57.23%) marginally precedes notAfter=12:15:00Z; attributed to bucket-boundary/clock skew, not reconciled.

ranked_hypotheses.title: External bank/PSP partner-side outage or rejection
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The bank-partner-api (external PSP) itself degraded or began rejecting traffic, so payment-service transfers fail. The mTLS/TLS cert-expiry error lines are the partner's response to our calls rather than our own cert having expired, and no internal service is at fault.

causal_chain.claim: External bank-partner-api begins rejecting/erroring on payment-service calls from ~12:12Z
Outbound transfer calls fail; bank_api_error_rate rises to 100% and success rate falls to ~2.4%
Failures are marked PENDING_RETRY, so the HTTP panel stays green

assumptions: The TLS cert-expiry log line refers to the partner's presented certificate rather than our client cert; but F20 explicitly names OUR client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal with notAfter 12:15:00Z, and F25 establishes the direction as the peer rejecting our cert (alert 45 to us).
No internal change is responsible (consistent with F7/F9/F14/F15).
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Directly contradicted by F20/F25: the rejected certificate is explicitly named as OUR client cert (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal, notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z) and the TLS alert 45 is received by us, i.e. the peer rejected our expired client cert rather than the partner's own outage causing the signature. No partner-side telemetry (F22/F28) supports a partner-origin fault.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Bad deployment: settlement-service v1.9.0 CSV exporter regression
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The lone deployment in the window (settlement-service v1.9.0, 'Batch settlement report export', new CSV exporter, dep-5510 at 10:30Z) introduced the fault, disturbing settlement/batch processing payment-service depends on or a shared component (ledger-db/kafka), so transfers stopped succeeding while the request/response error panel stayed green.

causal_chain.claim: settlement-service v1.9.0 deployed 10:30Z with a new CSV exporter
The new exporter disturbs settlement/batch processing
Disturbance propagates to payment-service fund transfers (via shared ledger-db/kafka or the settlement path)
Transfers fail silently as PENDING_RETRY, success rate collapses, HTTP panel stays green

assumptions: settlement-service shares a component or batch dependency with payment-service (not shown in the payment-service graph, F13).
The CSV-export change affects live transfer processing rather than only report exports.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Time-inconsistent (deployed 10:30Z, ~102 min before onset, F14) and mechanism-inconsistent: settlement-service is absent from payment-service's graph (F13), and the actual error signature is an mTLS cert rejection naming OUR client cert (F4/F20), which a CSV exporter change cannot produce. No unsupported-hop path survives.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Config change cfg-2502 (bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000) caused the failure
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The only payment-service change in the window, cfg-2502 raising bank.api.timeout_ms from 3000 to 5000ms at 11:20Z, altered outbound-call behavior toward bank-partner-api and caused the transfer failures and collapse in bank_api_error_rate/payment_success_rate.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2502 changes bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000 on payment-service at 11:20Z
Longer timeout shifts outbound calls to a broken/hanging path
bank_api_error_rate jumps and transfers fail silently

assumptions: A timeout increase could produce 100% failure and mTLS handshake rejections, which no mechanism in the evidence establishes.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Time-inconsistent (changed 11:20Z, ~52 min before the 12:12Z bucket and ~55 min before the first concrete error at 12:15:27Z, F14) and mechanism-inconsistent: the observed errors are mTLS handshake rejections of an expired client cert (F4/F21), not timeout-driven failures.

facts.statement: The earliest NEW error is at 12:15:27Z: 'payment 45f233b6 marked PENDING_RETRY: mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected'; the first TLS cert-expiry line follows at 12:16:44Z naming our client cert 'CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z', with 7 PENDING_RETRY and 5 expired-cert lines inside 12:15:00-12:20:00Z.

The rejected certificate is explicitly named in the logs as OUR client cert, and the TLS alert 45 direction shows the peer rejected our cert: 'bank-partner-api call failed: remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45); our client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z'.

payment-service bank_api_error_rate went from ~0.2% baseline to 57.23% in the 12:12Z bucket and 100% from 12:19Z onward (all buckets through 13:57Z), while payment_success_rate fell from ~99% to ~2.4-2.7% from 12:19Z — the same 12:12-12:19Z onset as the cert expiry.
The HTTP 5xx error_rate panel stayed flat/healthy at ~0.16-0.32% (mean 0.22) across 11:30-13:57Z, so the reported green dashboard is literally true for that metric.

No cert reload/renewal event exists: a 'reload' search over 12:15-12:20Z returned 0 matches and a 'renew' search over 12:00-13:59Z returned 0 matches; the expired-cert error was still logging at 13:58:39Z (171 ERROR matches in 12:14-13:59Z, all 'our client cert CN=payments-...').

No line anywhere describes the PARTNER's presented server certificate — no partner cert CN, issuer or notAfter exists in the matched output; the only partner-side information is the received TLS alert 45.

Both in-window changes are time-inconsistent with onset: cfg-2502 (payment-service bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000, 11:20Z) is ~52 min before the 12:12Z bucket and ~55 min before the first concrete error, and dep-5510 (settlement-service v1.9.0, 10:30Z) is ~102 min before onset.

Only one deployment (dep-5510, rolled_back_at null) and one config change (cfg-2502) exist in the entire window, and re-sweeping through 13:59Z returns the same counts with no compensating/rollback event; a payment-service-scoped config sweep for 12:00-13:59Z returns 0.

bank-partner-api is an external node with shared=false and has_telemetry=false whose only edge is payment-service -> bank-partner-api, so no other internal service consumes the affected component and no vendor-side telemetry exists; ledger-db and kafka are the shared components but are not on the failing path.

No certificate-inventory or lifecycle tool exists in this environment: queries for 'cert-inventory' and 'cert-lifecycle' returned not_found, and the known_services list contains no cert-management component.

A prior credential_expiry precedent exists in this environment: HIST-106 (2025-06-30, settlement-service mTLS cert expired) records root_cause 'Client certificate expired; no renewal automation' and resolution 'Issued new cert; added expiry alert'.
api-gateway, the upstream caller of payment-service, registered 0 WARN/ERROR logs in 12:00-12:40Z, and payment-service's only upstream edge is api-gateway -> payment-service (http).

recommended_actions.action: Immediately rotate/renew the payment-service client certificate used on the bank-partner-api edge (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal) — issue a new cert from the same CA/issuer, deploy it into payment-service's mTLS keystore, and reload/restart payment-service so the handshake uses the new material.
recommended_actions.rationale: The handshake is rejected as 'expired certificate (alert 45)' naming our client cert with notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z; every outbound transfer since 12:15:27Z has failed and the error persists through 13:58:39Z with no reload/renew event (F20, F25, F21, F23, F24). This is the direct mitigation.

recommended_actions.action: After reload, verify recovery on payment-service's bank-facing metrics: confirm bank_api_error_rate returns to ~0.2% baseline and payment_success_rate returns to ~99% in the next metric buckets, and confirm the 'expired certificate' ERROR lines stop.
recommended_actions.rationale: These two metrics are the diagnostic pair that detected the failure while the HTTP panel stayed green; success_rate at ~2.4% and bank_api_error_rate at 100% are the pre-fix state to reverse (F2, F3).

recommended_actions.action: Triage the PENDING_RETRY backlog: identify transfers marked PENDING_RETRY from 12:15Z onward and replay them once the mTLS handshake succeeds, confirming with settlement that no transfers were double-posted or lost.
recommended_actions.rationale: Failed transfers were not returned as 5xx but marked PENDING_RETRY on the settlement/retry path (7 PENDING_RETRY events in 12:15-12:20Z), so customer funds are sitting in a retry queue rather than having failed cleanly (F4, F5).

recommended_actions.action: Add payment_success_rate and bank_api_error_rate to the primary customer-facing payment dashboard, and alert on payment_success_rate dropping below its ~99% baseline — the HTTP error_rate panel must not be the only payment health signal.
recommended_actions.rationale: The HTTP 5xx error_rate panel stayed flat at ~0.22% while success_rate collapsed, because failures take a non-HTTP PENDING_RETRY path; the dashboard is structurally blind to this failure mode (F1, F3, F5).

recommended_actions.action: Add an explicit mTLS-handshake-failure / TLS-alert counter and error classifier for the bank-partner-api edge so cert-expiry rejections surface as a monitored signal instead of only as settlement-path ERROR logs.
recommended_actions.rationale: The only earlier evidence of the failure was low-level ERROR log lines (75 ERROR vs 1 WARN in 12:04-12:39Z) on a path that never increments the HTTP error metric (F4, F5, F24).

recommended_actions.action: Stand up certificate expiry monitoring and automated renewal for all service-to-service and bank/PSP mTLS client certs (alert at e.g. 30/14/7 days before notAfter), starting with the payment-service -> bank-partner-api edge.
recommended_actions.rationale: No cert inventory/lifecycle tooling exists in this environment (no 'cert-inventory' or 'cert-lifecycle' service), no renewal automation ran before the 12:15Z expiry, and the prior HIST-106 incident had the identical root cause 'Client certificate expired; no renewal automation' with remediation 'Issued new cert; added expiry alert' (F26, F23, F27, F29).

recommended_actions.action: Confirm the exact key/subject binding of the expired credential on the payment-service -> bank-partner-api edge and record it in an inventory once one exists; independently confirm with the bank partner that its truststore accepts the renewed cert.
recommended_actions.rationale: The cert-to-edge binding currently rests on a log-line parse, and no partner-side telemetry or cert registry exists to confirm it (F20, F22, F26, F28).

data_gaps: bank-partner-api could not be queried directly (tool not_found; external with has_telemetry=false), so the bank's own view of the TLS failure and any partner-side rotation/alert cannot be confirmed — only observed indirectly through payment-service logs and metrics (F10, F16, F28).

No logs were retrieved for order-service, settlement-service, notification-service, kafka or ledger-db, so a wider blast radius cannot be confirmed or excluded; ledger-db and kafka are shared components not on the failing path (F17).
The api-gateway log query returned 0 matches in the window; a broader INFO-level query was not run, so 'no errors' could not be distinguished from 'no logs at all' on the client-facing path.

No certificate inventory, issuance or renewal record store is reachable, so the cert-subject/key binding and the fleet-wide question (single cert vs many expiring certs) cannot be resolved from cert metadata; only the log-line notAfter remains as evidence (F26).

No log line describes the partner's presented server certificate, and the partner has no telemetry, so the alternative 'still-valid cert rejected / stale partner truststore' cannot be positively excluded — it is only left without positive evidence (F22).

Cert lifecycle events are not represented in the deployment/config-change feeds, so change-correlation alone cannot pinpoint the fault locus; the only two in-window changes are not time-consistent with onset (F14, F15).
No historical incident matched the exact symptom 'payment failures with a normal payment-service error dashboard', so this silent-failure pattern is not confirmed as a known precedent.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Evidence that the rejected certificate is NOT the one bound to the payment-service -> bank-partner-api edge (e.g. a cert registry or key-binding record showing a different subject/key for that edge), which would invalidate the core linkage of H1.

A log line or partner-side confirmation naming an expired certificate presented by bank-partner-api (partner server cert CN/issuer/notAfter), which would shift the root cause toward partner-side expiry.

Evidence that the partner was rejecting a still-valid client cert (e.g. handshake failure persisting after a verified renewal-and-reload, or partner truststore staleness), which would make the renewal action ineffective.

Discovery of a configuration, feature-flag, WAF or auth-service change at 12:12-12:19Z (outside the deployment/config feeds surveyed) that could produce mTLS handshake rejections, which would reopen the change-correlation hypotheses.

Evidence that shared ledger-db or kafka co-tenants degraded in the same window in a way that reaches payment-service, which would widen blast radius (though not change the origin or fix of the top hypothesis).
Recovery of transfers without any cert rotation (or a matching bank-side change that accepts the expired cert), which would falsify cert expiry as the necessary cause.

Direction of the cert check: the log phrase is 'remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45)' combined with 'our client cert ... notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z' — i.e. the peer rejected OUR client certificate as expired; the notAfter timestamp equals the reported expiry second and precedes the first rejection by 27s, which pins onset to the client-cert expiry rather than a still-valid-cert/truststore mismatch.

findings.statement: No certificate-inventory/lifecycle tool or service exists in this environment: queries for service 'cert-inventory' and 'cert-lifecycle' both returned not_found, and the returned known_services list (api-gateway, auth-service, order-service, portfolio-service, pricing-engine, market-data-service, payment-service, settlement-service, notification-service, exchange-gateway, ledger-db, user-db, redis-cache, kafka, exchange-api, bank-partner-api, kyc-provider, email-provider) contains no cert-management component.

No cert rotation or renewal job was attempted or deployed around/after the 12:15Z expiry on either side: the fleet-wide config sweep 2026-04-01T00:00Z–2026-04-02T13:59Z returns exactly one change (cfg-2502, payment-service bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000 at 11:20Z, author p.nair) and the fleet-wide deployment sweep returns exactly one deployment (dep-5510 settlement-service v1.9.0 at 10:30Z, rolled_back_at null). A payment-service-scoped config sweep for 12:00–13:59Z returns count 0.

bank-partner-api is an external, vendor-owned node with has_telemetry=false and shared=false, and its only edge is payment-service -> bank-partner-api; there is no second internal holder of that cert endpoint visible in the graph, so the bank-side rotation/renewal attempt cannot be observed (no telemetry from vendor side).

Historical cert precedent HIST-106 (2025-06-30, 'Settlement mTLS certificate expired', settlement-service) records root_cause 'Client certificate expired; no renewal automation' and resolution 'Issued new cert; added expiry alert', i.e. this environment has a prior credential_expiry incident whose remediation explicitly states renewal automation was absent — consistent with the current expiry happening without an automated rotation.

A second cert-adjacent precedent in the same search, HIST-108 (2025-10-01, auth-service 'Keys rotation published new key id before all pods loaded the JWKS'), is a rotation-mis-step with a different signature (401 invalid_token, users logged out) and is not a client-cert expiry; no rotation-related incident between 2026-04-01 and 2026-04-02 was returned, so there is no precedent of an in-window rotation attempt for payment-service.
